title: Same Tree
statement_short: Given the roots of two binary trees p and q, write a function to check if they are the same or not. Two binary trees are considered the same if they are structurally identical and the nodes have the same value.
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes in both trees <= 100, -10^4 <= Node.val <= 10^4
hint: Small node count (<= 100) allows simultaneous pre-order recursion to verify structure and values in O(n) time.
keywords: 0 <= number of nodes in both trees <= 100
why_not: Right: Tree DFS recursively compares current node values and recursively checks left and right subtrees in O(n) time and O(h) space. Not Tree BFS: Simultaneous level-order queue comparison works in O(n) time but requires extra queue memory overhead. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Hash tables do not preserve hierarchical parent-child structural relationships natively. Not Two Pointers: Scanning node pointer pairs directly is non-trivial without recursive or queue-based tree traversal.
